sense: in questions and after a negative
also: anything else I can do for you?

terms.gloss: anything (after a negative, and in questions that expect “no”)
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.101: nec vērō agere quicquam
Cic. Sen. 66: potest enim quicquam esse absurdius …?
terms.comment: “Not anything” is nihil, “and not anything” nec quicquam. After sī, nisi, num, nē, “anything” is quid (see something).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 7.11.2: quid agis? ecquid fit?
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: in impassioned questions, = num quid. As an adverb, “at all?”: ecquid audīs?, can you hear me? (Plaut. Aul. 269–270).

evidence: Ter. Ph. 151: Numquid … aliud mē vīs?
terms.comment: Numquid vīs? or Numquid aliud mē vīs?, anything else?, is the leave-taking of comedy.

phrases.latin: sed heus tū! quid agis? ecquid fit?
phrases.english: but hey, you! how are you? is anything happening?

phrases.latin: Numquid, Geta, aliud mē vīs? — Ut bene sit tibi.
phrases.english: Anything else you want from me, Geta? — Just that you’re well.

phrases.latin: potest enim quicquam esse absurdius quam, quō viae minus restet, eō plūs viāticī quaerere?
phrases.english: for can anything be more absurd than to pack more provisions the less of the road is left?
